**CLAIM** — session `session_017Qqyix2QcnpUC9XeYVDzx3`, branch `claude/issue-4467-impersonation-visible`.

**Ruling (delegated authority; open veto window)**: the audit-integrity framing is the priority — an admin doing ordinary work under someone else's identity, invisibly, corrupts attribution. The card's scope note is the fix's shape: `session.impersonatedBy` is already on the wire; the client identity state simply never refreshes and nothing renders it.

1. **Identity refreshes after impersonation state changes**: after the impersonate call succeeds (and after stop-impersonating), the client session/identity state must re-resolve — measure how the console holds identity today (the auth client/session hook in `packages/auth` + whatever app-shell context consumes it) and invalidate/refetch at both transitions. The shell then shows the IMPERSONATED user's name/avatar (that is what the session IS), and admin-only navigation follows the real session's privileges — the card measured Setup nav still rendering for a non-admin session; that must stop.
2. **A persistent impersonation banner** whenever `session.impersonatedBy` is present: names the impersonated user AND the impersonating admin, carries a stop/exit affordance calling `stop-impersonating` then refreshing identity. It must survive full SPA reboots (it derives from the session, not from client memory of the click). Placement: the shell chrome level where it is visible on every console page — measure where global banners/announcements already mount, follow that convention; if none exists, the header region is the home.
3. i18n per the live convention (all-ten-packs parity, inline defaults).

**Red-first**: mocked session carrying `impersonatedBy` → pre-fix no `/impersonat/i` text anywhere and the shell shows the pre-impersonation identity (the card's own probes — capture); post-fix banner present naming both parties, stop affordance wired, identity = session user, admin nav absent for a non-admin session. Must-not-change (green both sides): a normal session (no `impersonatedBy`) renders zero banner and identical chrome; stop-impersonating restores the admin identity and the banner disappears.

**Scope guard**: console-only — the server side is measured correct; do not touch data-objectstack or server-adjacent code beyond reading the session shape. If the identity-state home turns out to be shared with the Users page's impersonate action in a way that demands refactoring beyond state invalidation, report the measurement first.

**Grading**: patch `@object-ui/app-shell` (+ `@object-ui/auth` patch ONLY if the session hook needs a refresh method exposed — `.d.ts` measured; additive export → minor per precedent, say so). Never major.

**Surface (mutual exclusion)**: shell chrome/header + the impersonate action's call site (Setup Users page) + the session/identity state hook + tests + changesets. ⛔ NOT: `console/organizations/manage/**` (in-flight #4475), plugin packages (#4464/#4465), the test-support extraction (#4434), `content/docs/releases/`.

**RULING UPDATE (delegated authority; open veto window)** — the dispatched dev STOPPED correctly and the measurement falsifies my original ruling's premise. New ruling: **option A**, visibility work in the same PR.

**What the measurement established** (full detail in the dev's report): identity state is NOT stale — it re-resolves every SPA boot, to the ADMIN, because (1) the console authenticates every /api/ request with the localStorage bearer; (2) better-auth's bearer plugin server-side OVERWRITES the request's session cookie with that bearer, so the impersonation cookie never wins; (3) the impersonate action runs over the DATA lane, which — unlike the auth lane (`createAuthClient.ts:179`, the repo's ONLY reader) — never adopts the rotated `set-auth-token` the server hands back. The impersonated session token is dropped on the floor. **Impersonation is therefore a complete no-op in the console**, and the audit risk is the INVERSE of the card's framing: support staff believe they see a user's view while acting entirely as themselves.

**Why A** (on the delegated axes): the business pull is measured, not speculative — a shipped, metadata-declared support feature is inert. The defect is an ASYMMETRY between two lanes injecting the same credential, where one honors the server's declared rotation contract and one discards it — fixing it is one-contract-one-answer, not a new transport decision (that would be option B, rejected; C fossilizes the bug behind phantom-green pins; D alone is an upstream card this seat cannot land). A also makes the banner derive from the session the console actually authenticates with, so the indicator structurally cannot disagree with who the server thinks is acting.

**The A-scope** (one PR): (1) `createAuthenticatedFetch` mirrors the auth lane's 3-line `set-auth-token` capture — lane symmetry, no impersonation-specific logic in a generic lane; (2) `AuthProvider` exposes a refresh, invoked after impersonate/stop; (3) `impersonatedBy?` widens `AuthClientSession` (patch per the #4495 precedent — interface widening, not a new export); (4) the banner/exit/i18n exactly as originally ruled, now reachable; (5) **the exit affordance fails loudly** when stop-impersonating cannot restore (the server resolves the admin via the `admin_session` COOKIE — in cookie-blocked deployments the exit cannot work; it must say so, never appear to succeed). **Honest costs, recorded**: the admin's token is replaced in localStorage for the duration; a client that misses the stop rotation is stranded until re-login. Accepted as the price of the feature actually functioning; D (server refuses bearer-shadowed impersonation) is being filed in objectstack as defence-in-depth.

**Red-first correction** (the dev's warning is adopted): the mocked-`impersonatedBy` harness of my original ruling would be a phantom pin — a state production cannot reach. The primary pin is LANE-LEVEL: a data-lane response carrying `set-auth-token` rotates TokenStorage (currently RED — the header is ignored) beside the auth lane's existing green. Banner/exit pins ride on the session the refreshed identity actually returns; what the jsdom harness cannot drive (the live server round trip) is stated in-file, not faked.

#4304 is being closed as a duplicate of this card (one extra datum recorded there: its build saw no Impersonate entry point).
